journal:
We were sorting through some old photos the other day and my now wife laughed as she handed over one I don't think I'd ever seen before, she said she took it when she got back one night and I was passed out against the canvas, I did have a little bit of a drinking problem then, but I think more importantly I was burning the candle at both ends.

You see, I'd just had this bad idea about six months before to pack in my job and "do" art full time, well obviously now im much older its easy to see how stupid the idea was back then but twenty-something me was none the wiser. I'd been trying (and failing) to get exhibited for most of those six months, and I suppose you could say that artistically i'd started to lose my way, painting what was in vogue, changing up my style to suit particular clientele tastes. I had earned just enough doing comissions to pay my share of the bills, but it was clear I was fighting a losing battle.

I never really did sell many paintings, but I kept five or six of my favourite ones and brought them from house move to house move, I think the pme one in this photo might still be in the garage.
prompt: Low on the floorboards among paint tins, a desk lamp lights the face of a young man asleep against the wall beneath his finished canvas on easel, brush still loose in his fingers. The painting is something surreal and abstract
